chapter: Later views and life in Dallas
title: Fishing buddies and hunting
summary: Smith fishes with older companions, fished on Long Island, and says rabbits are gone from hunting.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Can you explain what the fun is? Do you like to be out in the countryside?
Yeah, I love it. I love being in the country. I get out there and turn on my radio. I always have me a buddy with me or something, and we turn on the radio...
A friend.
Yeah.
Who goes with you?

Sometimes I've got a lady or somethin' or other, or some man... Most of them's older men. Some of them are retired and they likes to fish, too. They'll stay as long as I'll stay. I'll pick them up and carry them on out there, and we
Buster Smith - 228
have our cots and things, lay down and rest, eat, cook...
You cook food?

Yeah. Get a stove, cook -- cook anything you want to cook. I got some buddies that are younger than me, and they go in and they stay two or three days and set out them great big what you call trap lines, and they go down there and they cook everything.
I wish I was staying longer. I'd love to come with you.
Eddie Durham said he was going to come down here and do the fishing with me. They all know about it. Basie know about it, too. And he ain't goin' fishing with nobody. I fished when I was in New York.
Basie couldn't go fishing. He's not well enough.
Yeah, I guess not. I fished when I was in New York. I went out to Long Island and fished.
Really?
Yeah. Sure did. I went and rented me a boat...
What about other forms of hunting? Do you do that, too?
No, I can't walk for it. I got (?) with my legs.
You used to do that, though..
Yeah.
What? Shooting?
Yeah. Well, I didn't shoot nothing but rabbit and squirrel. But now they got so you can't find no rabbit. No
Buster Smith - 229

rabbit. You can find a few squirrels. They're in town here. You see one of them down the street there every minute. But they don't allow you to shoot no squirrels in town. In fact, all the game out in the country there is all gone. With the rules, and the fox eat 'em up, the farmers' put all the stuff on the cotton to kill the cotton so he can pick it, and he don't have to have no cotton-pickers, I mean by hand -- he just picks it with a machine. And he pulls that stuff out of there, and leaves the sprinkling that kills the leaves. That kills the rabbit, too. The rabbit eats the leaves and it dies. The stuff is poisonous. They kill them. They killed out all the rabbits. You can't find a rabbit nowhere around here. You might find one around town here, but you get arrested if they catch you shooting out there.
